risks: The guard measures syntax, not runtime. A route could satisfy it by naming PrincipalDep and ignoring it. Acceptable because get_principal raises on a missing credential, but do not mistake the guard for a runtime proof; the API tests remain the behavioural evidence.

A bare mention of an auth alias is not authentication. Probe 3 confirms the detector is call-shaped at the primitive level, but route-level detection is a name test on annotations -- a route could annotate PrincipalDep and not use it. That is reviewable and rare; widening the detector to prove use would not be proportionate.
